binders: Arbitrary real speed c and point coordinates x,t.
conclusions: The proposition that q has temporal and spatial derivatives at (x,t) satisfying q_t+c*q_x=0 is equivalent to that exact same proposition under a second local name.
mathematical_definitions: Both named predicates expand verbatim to existence of real qt and qx with HasDerivAt in time and space and residual qt+c*qx=0.
Partial derivatives are encoded as one-variable derivatives with the other coordinate held fixed.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a positive real speed c, the two supplied notions of a field satisfying the one-way advection or transport equation at (x,t) are identical: each means that q_t and q_x exist there and q_t+c q_x=0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The positivity assumption on c is not used to distinguish the two predicates; their equivalence is definitional and would hold for any real c.
The result is pointwise at one arbitrary (x,t), not a global solution theorem.
It does not prove that the field satisfies the PDE; it only equates two names for the same predicate.
If the required derivatives do not exist, both sides are false and the equivalence still holds.
No traveling-wave profile q(x,t)=f(x-c*t), initial condition, propagation identity, uniqueness, or regularity beyond the local derivative predicate is encoded.
